title: The relative profinite test functor is a dense subsite over a geometric field
statement: For an algebraically closed field K [def-weil-algebraic-closure], the specified relative test functor S ↦ Spec(K) ×_{Spec Z} Spec LC(S,Z) [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor] is a dense subsite from profinite sets with their coherent topology to the small pro-etale site of Spec K [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]: it is cover dense, locally full and faithful, and a sieve is coherent-covering if and only if its image sieve is pro-etale-covering.

source.place: Examples 4.1.10 and 4.2.11; local-ring proof of the affine algebra calculation using Stacks Tags 092Q, 096D, 096T

proof.text: For a profinite S and a ring A, ring maps LC(S,A) to an A-algebra B are determined by restriction from LC(S,Z). Construct the inverse by LocallyConstant.liftPrimeSpectrum from the first coordinate of the LC(S,Z) prime-spectrum homeomorphism. Characteristic functions show equality after localization at every prime. Separate universes for S, A and B allow the integer coefficients without a universe mismatch. This gives the ring pushout from ULift Z and the isomorphism Spec LC(S,A) to the specified relative test scheme, with both projection equations.

Reuse the proved specMapEquiv and specMapEquiv_apply from ProEtalePointComponentsMaps for maps from an affine spectrum to Spec LC(S,Z), and relativeMapEquiv and relativeMapEquiv_target there for the relative pullback correspondence. Transport the affine source along the explicit test-scheme isomorphism and the homeomorphism Spec LC(S,K) with S. Reuse the imported profiniteProjection_natural to identify the spectrum projection after a target map. Thus the resulting Hom equivalence sends the specified functor map of f to f, giving full faithfulness for every field K. The connected-component correspondence itself is not needed.

For a weakly etale K-algebra B with K algebraically closed, absolute flatness makes every prime localization a field. Weak etaleness is preserved under localization and composition; the separable-algebraic field theorem and algebraic closedness make K to each such localization bijective. Therefore K to B identifies local rings. Absolute flatness writes each r as r*r*s; r*s is idempotent and has the same principal open as r, so Spec B is profinite. The explicit map LC(Spec B,K) to B supplied by liftPrimeSpectrum is bijective on spectra. LC is ind-Zariski, so its structural map identifies local rings; cancellation gives this for the explicit map to B. The proved RingHom.BijectiveOnStalks.bijective_of_bijective then gives the algebra isomorphism. These are the closed source APIs in WeaklyEtaleField, WeakDimension, PullbackProfinite, IndZariski and StalkIso.

For an affine pro-etale object U, put R = Gamma(U,top) and take the K-algebra structure induced by Spec.preimage of U.isoSpec.inv followed by its structural map. The weakly-etale Spec/algebra criterion makes R a weakly-etale K-algebra. Absolute flatness and the clopen basis make S = Spec R profinite. Apply the proved classification LC(S,K) isomorphic to R. The composite of U.isoSpec, the spectrum of that algebra isomorphism, and the explicit relative test-scheme isomorphism is over Spec K: its structural equation follows from the algebra isomorphism commuting with constants and the pullback second-projection equation. The cover-dense affine ind-etale basis consequently factors through the test functor, proving cover density.

Pull a covering sieve on a test scheme to the affine ind-etale subsite. Its finite jointly surjective refinement consists of arrows factoring through images of members of the original profinite sieve. The natural spectrum projections send their joint surjectivity to joint surjectivity of those profinite arrows. Reindex the finite family by Fin n to use the coherent-topology criterion. Conversely finite jointly surjective families give fpqc covers by profinite_test_object_functor, and all their scheme arrows are weakly etale. Thus the functor reflects and preserves covering sieves. Together with full faithfulness and cover density this is the required IsDenseSubsite structure.

theorem geometricFieldProfiniteDenseSubsite (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] :
    (profiniteToProEtOf (Spec (.of K))).IsDenseSubsite
      (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) (Scheme.ProEt.topology (Spec (.of K)))
